title: Add an audience role that rates the live explainer page
summary: Add an "audience" role beside the steward. It reads the live firstmate explainer page as a newcomer and records a 1–5 rating with evidence-cited findings. The steward's brief and `athena status` show the latest rating, and a rating of 2 or lower raises a steward work item. This retry leaves athena.toml and policy.rs untouched, which caused the earlier admission failure.

defaults_applied.how: Tests for the role, record, and fake-agent end-to-end run; clippy and fmt clean.
No email address or personal data in the record, code, or docs.
Drops the earlier README, architecture, and athena.toml changes to keep one focused change.
Record validation refuses bad ratings and findings without evidence.
Avoids the governance-file and policy.rs causes of the earlier failure.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Roles such as the steward are defined in code in roles.rs, not in athena.toml (grep of athena.toml found no steward role), so no athena.toml change is needed. This avoids the previous failure, which came from an unknown [audience] section.
Audience is the steward and owner, who judge whether shipped outcomes work for their readers.
The live explainer URL is a constant in the new audience module; no config schema extension is made.
Earlier prevention (a reading-time governance scan) was already tried; this reading instead avoids governance files entirely.

acceptance_criteria.text: An `audience` role definition exists in crates/athena-data/src/roles.rs with a goal, a fixed prompt and a cadence. The prompt tells it to read the outcome as its audience would, give a 1–5 rating, and cite evidence for every finding. It passes RoleDefinition::validate and its path is records/roles/audience-<n>.json.

A versioned, schema-tagged audience-rating record type holds the target (explainer page URL), the audience (newcomer), a rating (1–5 only), findings that each cite a source, and the time. Out-of-range ratings and findings without evidence are refused.

Run `cargo test`. Tests cover the role definition, record validation and round-trip, and an end-to-end run with the fake agent over a stubbed page, with no network access. It produces a rating record and the steward sees it.

Run `cargo test`. A test shows the steward's brief or `athena status` output includes the latest audience rating and findings, and that a rating of 2 or lower yields a steward work item. Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`; both are clean.

The role only reads and records; it changes no code or docs. The explainer URL default is defined in one place in code. No email address or personal data is added anywhere, and crates/athena-agent/src/policy.rs is unchanged.

athena.toml is not modified, and still parses with the existing schema. No new top-level section such as [audience] is added. If a change to athena.toml proves necessary, it must use only sections the schema already accepts.
docs/design/audience-role.md and a CHANGELOG entry describe the role, how to run it, where its records go, and how to add a target beyond the explainer.

out_of_scope: Changing the explainer page itself or any shipped outcome
Editing crates/athena-agent/src/policy.rs or its email allow-list
Auditing targets other than the explainer, beyond documenting how to add one
departures: Wider than the reference: this is a multi-crate change with new record types, steward and status wiring, and one prior failure at admission.
